notes: Hardening I traveler/cash bindings and Hardening II resident/non-resident bindings preserved. Hardening III adds summary.business, rules.business_invoicing_settlement, and rules.banking_conversion_practicality only. NG-B4 fields (country_overview, rules.exchange_controls) remain unbound. EFEMS/BDC/43-item temporal claims adopted but unbound. Legacy general CBN-approval / bank-only / availability formulations are forbidden by bound claim inferences.

bindings.wording_boundary: May summarize: statutory entry/exit declaration in excess of US$10,000 (operator >); that the declaration rule itself does not prohibit genuinely owned funds above that amount; and the FEMMPA s.14 physical-naira prohibition baseline with numeric traveller exception not established. Must not imply: declaration threshold is a carrying ceiling; unrestricted / without-limit foreign-currency carriage; any current numeric NGN exception (N10,000 / N20,000 / N100,000).

Declaration framing only for entry: cash/negotiable instruments in excess of US$10,000 must be declared. May note the CBN clarification that the declaration rule itself is not a prohibition on genuinely owned funds above that amount. Forbid: without limit; unrestricted; inferred carrying entitlement; declaration-as-ceiling.

May contain: statutory exit declaration in excess of US$10,000; statutory liable-on-conviction consequence for false/failed declaration; and the narrowly applicable FEMMPA s.21 cash domiciliary-account condition (cash-not-transfer retained). Forbid: amount declared on entry as universal ceiling; universal authorised-dealer documentation for every departing traveller; generic resident limits; declaration threshold equals carriage ceiling; softening 'liable on conviction' into 'may lead'.

Preserve dual-source roles explicitly: statutory MLPPA trigger remains in excess of US$10,000 (operator >) for entry and exit; Customs e-CDF operational trigger remains US$10,000 or more / >=. Do not flatten into one operator. Do not treat Customs >= as a formal amendment or interpretation of statutory >. Bind statutory rule as the legal threshold and keep Customs operational posture as a distinct companion claim.

May state: any person may open/maintain/operate a foreign-currency domiciliary account with an Authorised Dealer; denomination in internationally convertible currency; statutory source-disclosure non-obligation except as provided under any other enactment or law; multiple domiciliary accounts; exporters must maintain a separate export-proceeds domiciliary account; and banks must obtain identification evidence for domiciliary opening or wholesale cash/inter-bank deposits. Forbid: CBN limits and approval requirements as a general resident rule; prior CBN approval to open domiciliary accounts; equating KYC with CBN approval; general unrestricted access / unrestricted FX access / without-limit formulations; physical-cash entitlement from account opening; universal external-transfer rights; collapsing exporter and ordinary domiciliary classes; Form A or export cash-withdrawal rules from unpinned FX Manual 2026.

Must remain category-specific. May state: CDD external-account classes (diplomatic/IO); enumerated non-resident-account classes (correspondence/exam bodies; foreign companies on approved contracts; foreign professional bodies); closure on completion limited to CDD Reg. 25 subregulations (2) and (4); unclassified cases referred to CBN for clarification; Non-Resident Nigerians may own NRNOA/NRNIA subject to KYC (without prejudice to Memo 17); NRNOA remittance/dual-currency purpose; NRNIA investment purpose; NRNOA FCY balances fully repatriable without restriction; NRNOA Naira funding via offshore remittance or FCY conversion through authorised dealers. Forbid: all non-residents; more freely; transfer funds more freely; universal non-resident FCY entitlement; projecting NRN rights onto all foreign persons/entities; universal CBN approval; merging NRNOA and NRNIA; expanding NRNOA repatriation to NRNIA/all non-resident/investor/resident funds.

May summarize governed business FX architecture: statutory Market channels (Authorised Dealers and Authorised Buyers as distinct classes); documentation-backed Market purchase eligibility (not Form M/A schedules); inward investment via Authorised Dealer and Market conversion; investment-related dividend/profit and sale/liquidation transferability through Authorised Dealers; Market-purchased FX repatriation without further approval only within that prerequisite; and eligible NFEM classes processed by Deposit Money Banks under a non-exhaustive 'such as' framing. Must not imply: all significant FX transactions through authorised dealer banks; conversion only through authorised dealer banks; generic CBN approval for capital repatriation or certain payments; universal unrestricted repatriation; bank-only architecture; FX availability / scarcity / difficulty / poor rates / bank delays; free-floating or managed-float regime labels (NG-B4). Do not make the summary an exhaustive procedural manual.

Bind settlement/transaction mechanics only — not domestic invoicing currency rules unless separately established. May state: FEMMPA Market counterparty channels; documentation-backed Market FX purchase eligibility; inward investment via Authorised Dealer + Market conversion; CCI issuance and AD returns (including information required by CBN); unconditional transferability through Authorised Dealer of investment dividends/profits, loan servicing, and sale/liquidation proceeds within s.15 scope; Market-purchased FX repatriation without further approval (prerequisite retained); and s.27 export payment-mode conditions. Distinguish settlement channel from invoice currency. Forbid: generic Form M/Form A claims; generic CBN prior approval; capital repatriation requires CBN approval; certain payments require CBN approval; report-to-CBN as approval; conflating export domiciliary account (NG-ACC-05) with ordinary business settlement; universal unrestricted repatriation; principal/interest universal split beyond loan servicing.

Evidence-grounded operational conversion field only. May state: CBN may appoint Authorised Dealers and Authorised Buyers; Market transaction channels among those classes; transaction rate mutually agreed between purchaser and AD/AB; s.11 construction boundaries (not a macro tightly-controlled claim); and eligible NFEM transactions such as the CBN-listed classes processed by Deposit Money Banks. Forbid: subject to availability; conversion is difficult; FX is scarce; poor rates; bank delays; tightly regulated and often subject to availability; conversion only through authorised dealer banks; all significant FX through authorised dealer banks; free-floating / managed float / market-determined macro regime labels (NG-B4). Do not bind EFEMS interbank infrastructure or BDC architecture into this customer-facing conversion field.
